# A claim of mine that was wrong, and the five findings fixed beside it

The sixth review passed and found six things. One of them is a correction to this
journal, and it goes first because it is mine.

## F29: six of the seven, not seven

Note 324 and commit 227927e say that none of `core-no-io`'s seven IO libraries is
installed at this repository, and so that the clause "was carrying nothing". That is
wrong, and the reviewer measured it properly. `pg` is a declared dependency of
`packages/core`, `packages/core/node_modules/pg` is a link into the pnpm store, and a
`packages/core` import resolves from the importing package rather than from the
repository root. With the pre-fix configuration, `import { Client } from 'pg'` in
`packages/core/src` **is** refused by `core-no-io`, which I confirmed before writing
this: it reports
`node_modules/.pnpm/pg@8.23.0/node_modules/pg/esm/index.mjs`. Six of the seven were
silent, not seven, and the one that was caught is the one the criterion names by hand.

My measurement looked at the repository root, which is not where that import resolves
from, and I stated the conclusion in bold in a note and in a commit message where it
cannot now be edited. This record is the correction. The fix itself stands and was
always necessary: `bullmq`, `ioredis`, `undici`, `axios`, `got` and `node-fetch` were all
accepted before the anchoring and are refused after it, and red 322 proves `bullmq`.

The reason it matters beyond the arithmetic is the one the finding gives: a reader who
believes the `node_modules/` half of the alternation is dead weight could simplify the
pattern to the bare names and stop refusing the one library of the seven this repository
actually has, with both of this round's tests still green.

## F30: the negated literal, covered; the rest, written down

`money-as-integer-cents` read a literal with a decimal point in three positions and
missed the same literal behind a minus sign, which is how a credit line is written. The
rule now carries three more clauses for a `unary_expression` whose operand is that
literal, in the same three positions, and the tree stays clean under them. Three forms it
still does not read are now in its registry entry rather than left for a reader to
discover: exponent notation, which carries no decimal point; a parameter default, which
sits in none of the three positions; and an amount arriving as a string or a variable,
which no pattern can follow. All three are what SEEN-135's branded `Cents` is for, which
the entry already pointed at.

## F31, F32 and F33

F31 is F25's class in the paragraph beside it: a census of this ticket's own journal,
which the next coverage run overtook thirty-four minutes after it was written. It reads
"every coverage check in this journal" now, and says why a number was the wrong form.

F32 is the sharpest of the six. The CI step added for F23 reports success when the test
**skips**, and `StagedPathWithASpaceTest` skips wherever the workspace is absent, so
moving the step into the harness job, where it would read naturally beside the other
Python steps, would leave it green and the staged mode unexecuted, which is the state F23
described. The guard asserted only that the class name appears somewhere in the file. It
now splits the workflow into jobs, finds the one job holding the step, and requires that
job to install the workspace.

F33 restores an assertion the deleted `boundary.ts` carried and nothing replaced: that
the cloud SDK deny-list names every SDK its registry entry claims. Dropping `@aws-sdk/`
from the pattern left `rules --check` green, the fixture firing on another SDK and the
tree clean. The test now holds the pattern and the entry to each other in both
directions, and the entry's `google-auth-library` is corrected to the `google-auth` the
pattern matches.

## F34: the pair re-recorded

Checks 322 and 323 were recorded by hand without `--agent`, so the tdd record's entry
citing them passes only while `[routing] shadow` is true: with it off,
`_require_the_strictest_route_in_the_plan` would refuse a pair already in the journal,
which is exactly what SEEN-138's replay of finished tickets would read back. This round
records that pair again through `.harness-drafts/round8.sh`, which declares both the model
and the agent.

## And the review that closes this

On the founder's decision, the review that passes this ticket is Ruud's own. The reason is
structural rather than a matter of patience: a passing review record must carry every
finding resolved, six subagent reviews have each found between two and twelve things, all
of them real, and a seventh at full depth would find more. A person is in `[actors] tools`,
so `human:reviewer` satisfies the independence rule that `claude:reviewer` cannot, because
a Claude Code subagent inherits its parent's session id and the two merged precedents for
that, SEEN-111 and SEEN-113, both disclosed `self-review`. This is what SEEN-118's third
round being the founder's is for.
